title: Nearly 1,000 Arrested as Tear Gas and Clashes Escalate French Protests
snippet: French authorities made roughly 1,000 arrests on Saturday as nationwide demonstrations over high living costs turned violent in several cities, part of a broader wave of unrest sweeping Europe.
content:
French police deployed tear gas, water cannons, and heavy security measures on Saturday as nearly 1,000 people were arrested in a sweeping wave of nationwide demonstrations against high living costs and educational reforms, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

While many of the daylight rallies across France remained orderly, authorities reported late-day violence driven by radical groups. Security forces confiscated an assortment of weapons ahead of and during the rallies, including slingshots, lead pellets, fireworks, airsoft weapons, and even a katana.

Late-Day Escalation in Paris

In Paris, heavy pre-rally preparations left downtown streets quiet, with businesses boarded up and major public events preemptively canceled. Thousands gathered at Porte d'Italie after officials rerouted the main march away from the city center—a move union leaders slammed as authoritarian despite complying with the orders.

While the front line of the rally concluded peacefully, Nuñez reported that roughly 500 rioters embedded among thousands of radical activists clashed with police late into the evening. Paris prosecutors reported 64 arrests, primarily on charges related to possessing weapons or forming groups intent on violence.

Regional Violence and Political Flashpoints

Tensions flared outside the capital as well. In Orleans, thousands marched against a congress hosted by far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party as she launches her presidential bid. Demonstrators chanted slogans against both Le Pen and President Emmanuel Macron, referencing a recent lethal shooting in Trappes that Macron categorized as a racist terror attack.

In western and southern cities like Nantes, Lyon, and Marseille, riot officers used tear gas and water cannons to disperse groups breaking through police barricades or lighting street fires. Severe injuries were also reported, including a 20-year-old man in Toulouse who suffered severe hand injuries from an explosive device during the chaos.

For the first time, authorities noted the presence of far-right vigilante groups in cities like Cannes and Montpellier claiming to protect local businesses from radical left-wing militants.

Broadening Unrest Across Europe

The unrest in France reflects a continent-wide surge in public discontent over economic strain, corruption, and social policy:

  • Italy: Police arrested nine people and temporarily detained hundreds—many of them minors—during multi-city demonstrations. Troops were deployed to Milan to guard against looting.
  • Albania: Riot police in Tirana used water cannons against student protesters demanding lower tuition and calling for the prime minister's resignation.
  • Spain & Portugal: Thousands marched in Madrid over pension protections, while demonstrators in Lisbon rallied for affordable housing.

French protest groups, including the revived Yellow Vests, have already called for another wave of demonstrations and sit-ins outside government buildings on October 31 to oppose what they describe as the government's authoritarian drift.
